answer: Because the derivation is a one-way function of the quartz seed, the pigment timing is verifiable from the cipher record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 79 keys as a result pays 79 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 230 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is cheap once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
